content: Polyhomeotic-like protein 1 (PHC1) is a protein encoded by the PHC1 gene in humans. This gene is a homolog of the Drosophila polyhomeotic gene, which belongs to the Polycomb group of genes. The protein product of the PHC1 gene is a component of a multimeric protein complex that includes EDR2 and the vertebrate Polycomb protein BMI1. The PHC1 protein, the EDR2 protein, and the Drosophila polyhomeotic protein share two highly conserved domains, referred to as homology domains I and II. These domains are critical for protein-protein interactions and are believed to facilitate the heterodimerization of the PHC1 protein with the EDR2 protein. Mutations in the PHC1 gene have been implicated in cases of primary microcephaly, a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by significantly reduced brain size and associated intellectual disabilities (as referenced in DOI: 10.1093/hmg/ddt072). Additionally, PHC1 has been demonstrated to interact with other proteins, including BMI1 and PHC2, which are also members of the Polycomb group and are involved in chromatin remodeling and transcriptional repression.
